content:
Hi, I was surprised to find there is no simple notation for restrict, deleteEdges, induce, deleteVerts for SimpleGraph. I would like to start a discussion to decide on the notation for these operations in graph-likes by proposing the notation we have been using for Graph. I would very much welcome any input. Once there are enough candidates proposed, I will set up a poll.

Let F be edge set and X be vertex set. In the order of restrict, deleteEdges, induce, deleteVerts, we have been using G ↾ F, G \ F, G[X], G - X as the notation. I am pretty certain that people would be happy with G[X] as induce. G ↾ F comes from the notation for restriction in Matroid by @Peter Nelson.
deleteEdgesgets G \ F as

  1. It is the dual operation to /, contraction.
  2. One way to think about simple graphs is Set (Sym2 V) and set deletion naturally means deleteEdges.
    Lastly, deleteVerts gets G - X as its notation.

There is some nuance to about whether to use usual symbol or similar looking symbol. For example, my understanding is that G ↾ F is used as close enough substitute for G | F which is being used for set construction. I am hopeful that the right mix of precedence used in term parsing and scoped can allow us to use the usual symbols without trouble but I will wait for opinions of people who knows better about these things.
